Source: Git history, GitHub PRs, repository documentation.

Direct evidence for navigation rationale:

- PR #24, johnnylarner, 2026-10-08: “Native links avoid a routing dependency.” [PR](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/24)
- Documentation states: “Native document links keep browser history, reload, and new-tab behavior without a client router or another navigation state.” [docs/entity-details.md:94](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/docs/entity-details.md:94). Line 94 originates in commit `5ac298bf058e94c7aa395bceb84581e8f6afe476`; continuation remains in #46.
- The documented mechanism is explicit: “The frontend uses ordinary links and selects the page from the pathname when the document loads.” [docs/entity-details.md:72](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/docs/entity-details.md:72)

Circumstantial evidence:

- `frontend/index.html` has been unchanged since frontend introduction, commit `9336890` (#10, 2026-09-26). Its original HTML includes black `theme-color`, but no inline background styling or color-scheme.
- #24 introduced pathname-based page selection and links; #46 added summary/history pages. Their descriptions record functional navigation checks, without flash-specific testing. [PR #46](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/46)
- Inference: the flash is consistent with document navigation exposing an initially unstyled document. History supports the navigation mechanism, but does not prove the browser’s actual paint sequence.

Queries and coverage:

- `git log --all --oneline --regexp-ignore-case --grep='flash\|white\|flicker\|routing\|navigation'`
- File histories and pickaxe using `location.pathname|href=|background|color-scheme`.
- Complete bodies/comments/reviews for PRs #10, #24, #46; separate inline-review endpoints for #24/#46.
- GitHub PR searches `flash`, `white`, `flicker`, `routing`.
- Repository documentation search `flash|flicker|routing dependency|navigation|color-scheme`.

Gaps: No flash-specific PR, rationale, or discussion found. #10 has an empty body; all three PRs have no discussion/reviews. No contradiction found. Browser paint evidence remains outside this historical investigation.
